title: Boolean Functions
story: You're building a club entry system for a venue. Different rules for different areas: age checks for the main floor, temperature checks for the kitchen, ID checks for the bar.
why: Boolean functions answer yes/no questions. They're the decision-makers of your code — reusable checks that tell you whether something is true or false.
analogy: Boolean functions are like bouncers at a club — they check each person against the rules and say yes or no.
try_it: Write an `is_valid_username` function that returns true if a username has at least 3 letters AND at most 20 letters. Test it with short and long names.
tips: Use `&&` for AND and `||` for OR when combining multiple conditions
Boolean functions shine in `if` statements — `if is_adult(age)` is cleaner than `if age >= 18`
common_mistakes: Using `=` instead of `==` inside the function body: `return age = 18` is wrong
Forgetting to cover edge cases: does `is_adult(18)` return true? (It should if using `>=`)
Making functions too narrow — `is_13` is too specific; `is_teenager` covers the whole range
